rows.text: In the Garden of Life, as a trainer, you are checking on the little chimera's work.
rows.speaker: Simulated Universe

rows.text: "Your performance is below standard again today. Can't you learn from your coworkers and try to keep up with their task progress?" You interrogate the little chimera.
rows.speaker: Simulated Universe

rows.text: "But... boss, keeping up with the schedule is impossible!" The little chimera begins to argue for itself, "Because to catch up with other coworkers' progress, I first need to catch up with the current progress. But once I catch up with the current progress, the others will have moved even further ahead!"
rows.speaker: Simulated Universe

rows.text: "At this rate, I'll never catch up with my coworkers!" The little chimera declared blatantly.
rows.speaker: Simulated Universe

rows.text: Moved by this well-reasoned argument, you decide to ease up on employee performance metrics. The little chimera beams gleefully.
rows.speaker: Simulated Universe

rows.text: The little chimera has a point, and you quickly find a way to solve the problem:
rows.speaker: Simulated Universe

rows.text: Why not just give other chimeras time off and let the little chimera who's behind schedule continue working? Working while others are on holiday is also a form of overtime. You've dubbed this method the "Theory of Relative Overtime."
rows.speaker: Simulated Universe

rows.text: "What's all this mumbo-jumbo?" You couldn't understand the little chimera's reasoning at all, but you know one thing for sure: No food to eat if today's work isn't finished!
rows.speaker: Simulated Universe
